TOP OF BOOK

  • UBS GROUP (UBS / UBSG SW) [DELTA ▲] — Q2 2026: net profit $2.8bn (+17% YoY), record Global Markets quarter; new $3bn buyback announced, beating the $1.5bn consensus expectation.
    • Vs. baseline: Net profit of $2.8bn beat the AWP consensus of $2.38bn, driven by investment banking. Investment bank revenues jumped 26%, with the bank calling it "a record second quarter" for global markets. The new $3bn buyback — double what the Street was pencilling — starts immediately with at least $1bn in the next three months, running through Q2 2027.
    • Read: The buyback size is the non-consensus item here — the market had been watching for $1.5bn alongside potential Swiss regulatory capital relief of roughly $3bn; instead UBS delivered $3bn, a strong signal that CS integration capital generation is ahead of plan. The bank says it remains on track to exceed its 15% capital return exit rate by 2026, but pace of future buybacks depends on the outcome of Swiss capital regulations. GWM attracted $36bn in net new assets; cumulative CS integration savings hit $12.6bn, integration on track for end-2026. Risk: Swiss parliament's Economic Affairs Committee pushed its banking law revision decision to August 2026, full floor vote not before September — the regulatory capital surcharge on foreign subsidiaries remains live and could constrain the next buyback tranche. Leg: equity bullish (buyback double consensus), AT1/T2 neutral. Action: add on any early pullback, keep Swiss capital law on monitor.
    • Sources: Bloomberg | Investing.com | Yahoo Finance/AFP
  • DEUTSCHE BANK (DBK GY) [DELTA ▲] — Q2 2026 TODAY: net profit €1.64bn, +10% YoY, beating consensus of €1.38bn; new €500mn buyback; NII guidance raised to above €14bn.
    • Vs. baseline: DBK posted a 10% Q2 profit rise to €1.64bn, defying expectations for a decline, as investment banking offset higher expenses; the consensus was €1.38bn. Q2 net revenues €8.5bn, H1 net revenues €17.2bn; H1 post-tax profit €4.1bn — the highest half-year result in the bank's history. A new €500mn buyback from 2026 net income was announced, with CET1 ending the quarter at 13.9%. NII guidance lifted slightly to above €14bn for FY2026.
    • Read: Shares closed down ~0.4% despite the beat — classic sell-the-news on a name where consensus had already moved; the stock reaction (+8.24% EPS surprise but -2.91% stock move) tells you positioning was full going into the print. Management flagged CRE as "planned de-risking" in Q2 — the portfolio remains "resilient" but this is worth probing on the fixed income call today (30 July). 20 consecutive quarters of revenue growth removes the bear case; incremental buyback acceleration now the only equity catalyst. NII guidance above €14bn is a positive read for net interest spread trajectory into H2. Leg: equity neutral on day (priced), credit/AT1 stable. Action: monitor CRE commentary from today's fixed income call; no new position at current entry.
    • Sources: RTÉ | Investing.com transcript | DB IR
  • UNICREDIT / COMMERZBANK (UCG IM / CBK GY) [DELTA ▲] — German government shifts from blocking to negotiating; Orcel signals Q4 2026 close possible; formal talks resuming post-CBK earnings on 6 August.
    • Vs. baseline: Germany's Finance Ministry has reversed from outright opposition, stating it is "now up to the two banks to talk," signalling a shift in Berlin's stance — though the ministry retains objections to the pace and approach of UCG's acquisition strategy. Orcel told Corriere della Sera he sees room for an agreement, stating "all concessions we were prepared to make are still intact." Orcel is expected to meet CBK CEO Bettina Orlopp after Commerzbank reports on 6 August. Orcel told CNBC the acquisition could "potentially" close in Q4 2026. Background: UCG secured 47.6% of CBK shares after the tender, well ahead of original expectations.
    • Read: Berlin's pivot is the NEW element — the blocking posture has collapsed. The transaction frame has shifted from "if" to "terms." Key binary: CBK 6 Aug earnings print. If CBK delivers another beat and lifts targets, Orlopp's negotiating position hardens; a miss accelerates capitulation. Long CBK equity on deal spread compression is the obvious trade, but regulatory/supervisory sign-offs (ECB, BaFin) and Commerzbank board resistance are still friction. UCG's proposed CBK strategy would cut the international network and focus on Germany and Poland — a post-merger restructuring would compress CBK's NII contribution and alter its funding profile; CBK's CDS and AT1s may widen if market prices in post-merger structure risk. Action: long CBK / short HVB credit on deal gap compression; monitor 6 Aug CBK earnings as next binary.
    • Sources: Bloomberg | CNBC | UCG IR

BY NAME / THEME

  • BARCLAYS (BARC LN) [DELTA ▲] — Q2 reported 28 July: income £8.3bn (+16% YoY), PBT +31% to £3.25bn, £1bn buyback, 2026 income guidance raised to ~£31.5bn.
    • Vs. baseline: NII £3.92bn beat estimate of £3.84bn; IB revenue £3.96bn beat estimate of £3.66bn significantly; FICC £1.47bn slightly missed £1.51bn estimate; £1bn buyback announced. 2026 income target raised to ~£31.5bn — this is a delta vs. the prior guide. Capital distributions for H1 reached £2.3bn (+61% YoY); CET1 stable at 14.3%. Completed 2026 capital issuance plan (including inaugural A$1bn AT1 and £750mn T2); MREL plan completed in H1.
    • Read: IB beat is the surprise, FICC the miss — consistent with the US bulge bracket pattern this quarter. IB advisory fees +51% and ECM income +91% YoY — the deal pipeline is clearing. Credit impairment charges rose 22% to £571mn — consensus unemployment expectations consumed Q1 post-model adjustments; watch consumer credit through H2. NII outperformance of £3.92bn vs. £3.84bn estimate signals resilient UK rate sensitivity; MREL plan completion removes 2026 issuance risk and tightens senior spread technicals. Leg: equity positive (guidance upgrade), AT1 stable/positive (MDA headroom ample), senior/T2 stable. Action: hold/add equity on IB leverage; AT1 no action needed.
    • Sources: Yahoo Finance | LiveSquawk
  • UNICREDIT (UCG IM) [DELTA ▲] — Q2 reported 23 July: record €3.1bn net profit, 22nd consecutive record quarter; 2026 guidance raised to ~€11.5bn ex-integration costs.
    • Vs. baseline: H1 net profit €6.1bn, up 24% adjusted, RoTE 24%; FY26 guidance raised to well above €11bn, or ~€11.5bn ex-integration costs. UCG warned of a ~€140mn extraordinary hit from Banca Progetto and Rover (Romania) — new item, not in consensus. Shares fell 4.72% on the day despite the print — market focused on deal risk, integration costs, and elevated capital deployment into CBK.
    • Read: The sell-off on a record print is the signal: the market is pricing deal execution risk (€22bn CBK commitment) at a significant discount to the fundamental run-rate. If Berlin negotiation de-risks further, the UCG discount unwinds. The Banca Progetto hit is small but flags that the "no surprises" streak has ended. CBK deal funding would consume capital that would otherwise support NII growth and buybacks, compressing UCG's near-term capital return capacity. Leg: equity — buy the deal-discount dip if CBK talks progress; AT1/T2 stable with RoTE 24% providing ample cushion. Action: monitor CBK deal progression; 6 Aug CBK print is the next re-rating trigger.
    • Sources: UCG IR | Investing.com transcript
  • BNP PARIBAS (BNP FP) [DELTA ▲] — Q2 reported 23 July: net profit €4.35bn (+33%), revenues +12%; CET1 13% hit one year early.
    • Vs. baseline: Net profit €4.35bn beat consensus of €4.21bn by ~€140mn; the 33% jump includes an €858mn gain from the AGI/Ageas transaction. The CET1 target of 13% — set for 2027 — was reached in Q2 2026, a year early. Equities trading hit record revenue; FICC remained flat, lagging US peers. Operating expenses rose 10%, flagged as a "weak spot" by analysts.
    • Read: Early CET1 achievement paves the way for accelerated distribution, per management — the watch is for a special or bumped buyback announcement at Q3 or FY. Underlying ex-Ageas beat was smaller; FICC flatness is consistent with ECB rate holds reducing European rates volatility and compressing NII contribution from fixed income businesses. Cost trajectory is the genuine risk to 2027 earnings revisions — AXA IM integration impact on jaws is a known headwind. Leg: equity positive (CET1 optionality), credit stable. Action: monitor for distribution announcement; no new position on AXA IM cost drag.
    • Sources: BNP IR press release | Investing.com
  • SANTANDER (SAN SM) [IN LINE] — Q2/H1 reported 23 July: underlying H1 profit €7.33bn (+15%); on track for >€14.1bn FY guidance; ECB-approved €1.8bn buyback.
    • Vs. baseline: Record underlying H1 profit of €7.33bn, up 15%, with the ONE Transformation driving lower costs. ECB approved a €1.8bn buyback against H1 2026 results. TSB acquisition closed 30 April, bringing 4mn customers and £400mn+ expected cost synergies. Binary resolved in-line — no deviation from the trajectory.
    • Read: TSB integration execution is now the key watch item. UK mortgage repricing cycle and credit normalisation in Brazil are the two vol-generating segments for H2 — both carry NII and impairment charge implications into H2 guidance. ECB buyback approval removes that bureaucratic risk. Leg: equity neutral (priced), AT1 stable. Action: no action; monitor UK consumer credit quality through H2.
    • Sources: Santander IR | Yahoo Finance
  • ADYEN (ADYEN NA) [NEW] — CFO Ethan Tandowsky departing effective August 2026; H1 2026 results on 13 August.
    • Vs. baseline: Tandowsky departure effective August 2026; successor search initiated. This was not in the prior AM run. H1 2026 results publish 13 August. Last known Q1 print: net revenue €620.8mn (+16% YoY, +20% constant currency), processed volume €382bn (+21%). Guidance: 20–22% constant currency revenue growth for FY2026; EBITDA margin broadly in line with 2025.
    • Read: CFO transition into a H1 print is an execution risk overhang — management continuity and forward guidance credibility will be scrutinised. The Talon.One acquisition (~€750mn, Orb acquisition also announced June) adds integration complexity alongside the leadership gap. Adyen has historically re-rated sharply on guidance changes; H2 guidance at the 13 Aug call is the catalyst. Funding costs for acquisitions and FX translation on non-EUR processed volumes are the principal financials transmission risks into the H1 print. Leg: equity — flag and monitor. Action: reduce ahead of 13 Aug on CFO transition risk; re-enter post-print if H2 guide lands in-range.
    • Sources: Adyen IR | Quartr

CREDIT CORNER

  • BARCLAYS — AT1 / MREL ISSUANCE COMPLETE [IN LINE] — 2026 capital plan finished; potential pre-funding of 2027 on the table.
    • Barclays completed its 2026 capital issuance plan, including an inaugural A$1bn AT1 and a £750mn T2, and completed its £10bn MREL target in H1 amid supportive credit market conditions. The bank may consider pre-funding 2027 issuance depending on market conditions. Read: No forced supply risk for the rest of 2026. Pre-funding signal is positive for BARC senior/T2 spreads — incremental demand without urgency. Action: overweight BARC senior NP on spread tightening bias.
      • Sources: Yahoo Finance | LiveSquawk
  • EUROPEAN PRIVATE CREDIT / CLO MARKET [NEW] — European private credit CLO market "sparked back to life" (Creditflux, 3 July); Ares Capital Europe VI ($20bn) and CVC European Direct Lending IV ($12.2bn) the two largest recent fund closings.
    • Ares Capital Europe VI LP ($20.01bn) and CVC European Direct Lending IV ($12.17bn) closed as two of the three largest private credit fund closings of 2025. New direct lending CLO issuance in Europe is resuming after a lull. Read: Capital deployment pressure from mega-fund closings will push spreads tighter in European direct lending through H2 2026 — watch for compression in upper mid-market deals vs. BSL. Bank SRT pipelines remain active as primary banks offload LBO risk into the private credit wrapper, reducing risk-weighted assets and improving capital ratios. Action: monitor spread compression in direct lending vs. BSL; flag for bank SRT deal flow read-through.
    • Sources: S&P Global | Creditflux
  • EUROPEAN CRE [DELTA ▲] — Q2 2026 investment volumes €53bn (+6% YoY); seventh consecutive quarter of value gains.
    • European real estate investment volumes rose 6% to €53bn in Q2 2026, with investors favouring living assets despite geopolitical uncertainty, per Savills. European CRE logged a seventh straight quarter of value gains, with stronger rental income offsetting higher yields and investor caution. Read: Volume recovery reduces bank CRE provisioning pressure modestly — relevant for DBK (which flagged planned CRE de-risking in Q2), and indirectly for Barclays and BNP with legacy office books. Stabilising collateral values support loan-to-value ratios on existing CRE books, reducing expected credit loss provisions and providing modest NII relief on refinancing activity. Office vacancy bifurcation (prime vs. secondary) persists. This is a slow-burn positive, not a catalyst. Action: monitor; inform DBK CRE provision trajectory into Q3.
    • Sources: CRE Herald/Savills
